Dear Priya,

Thank you for your message. In the third quarter of 2026 (July to September), the LCI India Focus Equity Fund A-Acc-USD share class returned -5.4% in USD, compared with -4.1% for its benchmark. The portfolio manager's Q3 2026 commentary explains that Indian shares fell as foreign investors sold, the rupee weakened against the US dollar and lenders reported higher bad-loan provisions. The largest detractors were Bharatvani Bank, Indrapat Finance and Vindhya Realty.

Past performance is not a reliable indicator of future returns. The value of investments and the income from them can go down as well as up and you may get back less than you invested.

Kind regards,
Client Services Team, Lumen Crest Investments

Dear Meera,

As of 30 September 2026, the ongoing charges figure (OCF) for the LCI Global Technology Fund is 1.89% a year for the A-Acc-USD share class and 1.04% a year for the Y-Acc-USD share class. The OCF is the annual cost of running the fund and is already reflected in the share price.

Kind regards,
Client Services Team, Lumen Crest Investments

Dear Sunita,

Thank you for getting in touch. We are not able to give personal investment advice. If you are unsure whether an investment is right for you, please speak to a financial adviser.

For information, the LCI India Focus Equity Fund has a risk indicator of 6 out of 7 and invests in a single country, so its value can rise and fall sharply. The income from it is not guaranteed.

Kind regards,
